quote: Theorem 3.9. Let {U1, . . . , Un} and {V1, . . . , Vn} be two sets of independent random variables with Ui ~ F̄(x; αi) and Vi ~ F̄(x; βi), respectively. Also, let {J1, . . . , Jn} and {J1*, . . . , Jn*} be another two sets of independent Bernoulli random variables, independently of U_i's and V_i's with E(Ji) = pi and E(Ji*) = p*i, respectively. Further, let N1 and N2 be two positive integer-valued random variables independently of T_i's and T_i*'s satisfying N1 ≤st N2, respectively. Assume that the following conditions hold: (i) F̄(x; αi) is decreasing and convex in αi for all x; (ii) ψ : (0, 1) → (0, ∞) is a differentiable, strictly decreasing convex function. Then, for (ψ(p), α; n), (ψ(p*), β; n) ∈ Mn, we have (ψ(p*), β; n) = (ψ(p), α; n)T ⇒ TN1:N1 ≥st TN*2:N2.
